o.text: From Proto-Turkic *tïŋla-, *tiŋle- (“to listen”), derived from Proto-Turkic *tiŋ (“reason, mind”). Compare Old Turkic 𐱃𐰃𐰭𐰞𐰀 (tïŋla-, “to listen”). Cognate with Turkish dinlemek, Turkmen diňlemek, Tatar тыңлау (tıñlaw), Kazakh тыңдау (tıŋdaw), Uzbek tinglamoq, Chuvash тӑнла (tănla).
From Proto-Turkic *kara. Cognate with Old Turkic [script needed] (kara, “black”), Turkish kara, Chuvash хура (hura), etc.

From Proto-Common Turkic *ūčuz, cognate with Old Turkic [script needed] (učuz, “easy”), Karakhanid اُجُزْ (učuz, “worthless”), Turkish ucuz, Turkmen ujyz, Tatar очсыз (oçsız), Bashkir осһоҙ (ushuð, “cheap”), Southern Altai очы (očï, “small”), etc.
From Ottoman Turkish مدنیت (medeniyet, “civilization”), from Arabic مَدَنِيّ (madaniyy, “urban; civilized”), from Arabic مَدِينَة (madīna, “city”).
